$comment: Haggling is rock-paper-scissors against a stance the customer telegraphs. Countering forces a stance change, so you are reading a moving target and cannot mash one button.
$visitComment: Chance a given customer turns up on a given day, rolled from a seed derived from (customer, day) so a visit is a fact about the day rather than a re-render.
$budgetComment: Total width of the purse variation, centred on the customer's budget multiplier — 0.35 means roughly ±17%. Without it every visit offered an identical ceiling and haggling became arithmetic the player had already done once.
$actionComment: Each family counters exactly one stance and backfires against exactly one other. The backfires are thematic, not arbitrary — lecturing a noble, flattering someone in a hurry, offering a freebie to a sceptic.
$holdFirmComment: Outside the triangle. Costs patience heavily and converts accumulated interest straight into ceiling — worthless early, decisive once two counters have landed. Knowing when to stop pitching and close is the skill ceiling of the whole system.
$palateComment: `wants` is what this person always asks for by name. `palate` is their taste, and it is what makes a walk-in interested in a potion nobody wrote them a line for — anything within spreadDeg of the palate is something they would consider. Without it a customer only ever bought from a list of one or two, so brewing anything else had no buyer but the shelf.

roster.$comment: Village remedies: clean water and honest earth. The widest taste on the roster, because a villager will try anything that grows nearby — which is also what stops a murky, marginal recipe like the Mirebloom Elixir from having no buyer in the world at all.
Heat and hardiness — what you drink before a watch.
Refinement with a shadow in it. Wide purse, narrow taste.
Buys only the dark work, and pays not to be asked about it.
